findings.title: No-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not exist
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added on UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). There is no zero-arg overload in this class or its parents, so this change does not compile and the passkey re-authentication fix cannot build. The call needs to match the actual method (for example passing context.getUser()), and that method must not require a non-null user if it is also used for the anonymous login page.

findings.title: Passkey UI only filled when user is already set
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() returns true only when webauthnAuth is present, realm passkeys are enabled, and user != null. authenticate() and the error challenge() now use that helper as the only place that calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(), after the previous user == null setup was removed. On the initial username/password (and username-only) page the user is still null, so the conditional WebAuthn form, challenge, and autocomplete attributes are never set and passkey login cannot start. The same gate drops the passkey UI on a failed password challenge, because badPasswordHandler runs while context.getUser() is still null (the user is only attached in validateUser after the password check, and is cleared on failure). Re-authentication is the only path that still gets the WebAuthn form. The condition should be passkeys enabled regardless of whether a user is already selected, which is what the existing login tests still assert via //form[@id='webauth'] on the first page.
